description: GASP conformance set for Apache Ossie: one case per construct OSSIE_SQL_2026 cannot state (the staged reasons in the GASP export) and the cases for a direct expression over a snapshot dataset, each with a complete model, a standard SQL reference query, the expected result on the GASP fixture and the rows it reads. A case with readings also lists the values a query returns under each named mistake or alternative reading. Written by npm run conformance in gasp-wiki-mcp.

grading.alternative: A value listed with grade alternative: a reading other tools take and GASP does not. Report it by name.
grading.wrong: Any other value. When it equals a value listed with grade wrong, the mistake is the one named there.
grading.failed: No value: the implementation rejects the model or the query, or the query errors.

customer.slice: snapshot rows on month starts, month ends and the period bounds shifted back by one, three, six and twelve months; on 2026-02-08, 2026-02-09, 2026-03-08, which a case off the calendar month reads; on every date from 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30, which a listed reading sums across

invoice.slice: snapshot rows on month starts, month ends and the period bounds shifted back by one, three, six and twelve months

opportunity.slice: snapshot rows on month starts, month ends and the period bounds shifted back by one, three, six and twelve months

subscription.slice: snapshot rows on month starts, month ends and the period bounds shifted back by one, three, six and twelve months; on every date from 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30, which a listed reading sums across

user.slice: snapshot rows on month starts, month ends and the period bounds shifted back by one, three, six and twelve months

cases.construct: a cohort fixed at the opening of the period and followed through its events (Net Revenue Retention)
cases.formula: (metric.mrr at period_start + metric.expansion_mrr - metric.contraction_mrr - metric.churned_mrr) / metric.mrr at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

cases.construct: the same aggregate one period earlier (period-over-period growth)
a snapshot read at the opening of the period beside events inside it
cases.formula: metric.churned_customers / metric.total_customers at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

readings.name: closing_value
readings.description: the customers active on the last day of the period as the denominator, where the formula reads the first day

cases.construct: a share of the ungrouped total inside a breakdown
the reporting period bound to a field other than the dataset's time field (opportunities by close date on a snapshot)
cases.formula: count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost') and in_period(field.close_date))

readings.name: period_on_snapshot_date_only
readings.description: the opportunities as they stand at the period end with no bound on the close date, so the period reaches the dataset's time field alone and every deal ever closed is counted

cases.construct: an aggregate cumulative from the start of history to the period end
cases.formula: count_distinct(field.ticket_id where field.ticket_status in ('open', 'pending')) at period_end

cases.construct: the number of days in the reporting period as a value
a dimension defined by ranges over a per-row expression
trailing windows of different lengths ending at the period end (one day over thirty)
a count of distinct tuples (account and feature pairs)
an unbounded range beside a bounded one (users who signed up in the period, active any time after)
cases.formula: all_time(count_distinct(field.user_id where field.product_event_type = 'qualifying' and in_period(field.signup_date) and (field.event_date - field.signup_date) = 30)) / count_distinct(field.user_id where in_period(field.signup_date))

cases.construct: a sum over a snapshot dataset for a month, read on the last snapshot date of the month

readings.name: summed_over_every_date
readings.description: the sum taken over every snapshot date in the period, so each subscription is added once per day

readings.name: opening_value
readings.description: the sum on the first snapshot date of the period, where the formula reads the last

cases.construct: a sum over a snapshot dataset for a quarter, read on the last snapshot date of the quarter

readings.name: month_ends_summed
readings.description: the closing value of each month in the period added together, where the formula reads the closing value of the last

readings.name: opening_value
readings.description: the sum on the first snapshot date of the period, where the formula reads the last

cases.construct: a distinct count over a snapshot dataset for a month, read on the last snapshot date of the month

readings.name: distinct_over_every_date
readings.description: the distinct count taken over every snapshot date in the period, so a customer active on any day of it is counted, one who left before the last day included

readings.name: rows_over_every_date
readings.description: the active rows on every snapshot date in the period counted without DISTINCT, which gives customer days

readings.name: opening_value
readings.description: the count on the first snapshot date of the period, where the formula reads the last

cases.construct: the opening value of a period that begins on the day a customer starts, read from the snapshot dated on the first day of the period
cases.formula: metric.churned_customers / metric.total_customers at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

readings.name: prior_period_close
readings.description: the opening value read from the last snapshot date before the period (the prior period's close), which leaves out the customer who starts on the first day
